The '''1991–92 season''' was the 61st season for '''[[Real Madrid C.F.]]''' in [[La Liga]].

==Summary==
During the summer, President [[Ramon Mendoza]] appointed [[Radomir Antic]] as head coach for the upcoming season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2020/04/07/football/radomir-antic-atletico-barcelona-real-madrid-spt-death-spt-intl/index.html|title=Radomir Antic, the only man to coach Barcelona, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, has died|first=Ben |last=Church|website=CNN|date=7 April 2020 |access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref> On 8 October 1991 Mendoza appointed [[Leo Beenhakker]] as club manager until 1994.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1991/10/09/deportes/686962817_850215.html|date=9 October 1991|accessdate=8 January 2025|publisher=elpais.com|language=es|title=Beenhakker was in Madrid to sign his new contract}}</ref> 

Real Madrid won no trophies for the second season in a row. Real Madrid lost the league title to [[Barcelona]] on the final day of the campaign after a 3–2 defeat against [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]]. Serbian coach [[Radomir Antić]] was suddenly sacked in January despite Real Madrid leading the league in the standings. On 30 April 1992, the club and Mexican striker [[Hugo Sanchez]] agreed to end their contract and parted ways after seven years.

Real lost the [[1992 Copa del Rey Final|Copa del Rey final]] to [[Atlético Madrid]] and also exited the [[1991-92 UEFA Cup]] after a loss to [[Torino FC|Torino]].
